### Observed differences

- A01 was completely absent in the earlier window (0 of 200 traces) and appears in the later window exactly once in every trace (200 of 200, never twice in one trace). A09 shows the reverse: it ran in 90 of 200 traces (45 in 100) before and in none of the 200 traces after. [OCC001, OCC007]
- A01 sits early in the case: its median position in the later window is 0.2 of the trace (mean 0.29). A09 previously sat at the very end (mean position 1.0). [POS001, POS008]
- Routing into A01 changed: before, A02 led almost exclusively to A04 (about 87 in 100 of its outgoing transitions) and never to A01; in the later window A02 leads to A01 in 54 in 100 and to A04 in 44 in 100. A04, which previously never led to A01, now does so in about 39 in 100 of its outgoing transitions, while its shares towards A03, A05, A07 and A10 all shrank. From A01 the flow continues mostly to A04 (about 46 in 100 of A01's outgoing transitions), otherwise to A07, A03, A10, A05 or A08, with small new edges into A01 also from A05, A07 and A08. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, DIR005, DIR007, DIR008]
- Before, A01 shared no traces with any activity; in the later window it co-occurs with each of A02, A03, A05, A06, A07, A08, A10 and A11 and precedes them in nearly every shared trace (e.g. before A03 in about 46 of 100 traces overall, roughly 19 of 20 shared cases). The exception is A04: A01 comes before A04 in 55 of 100 traces and after it in 45. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010]
- The ending changed: before, A06 (median position 0.8) was always directly followed by A09, which closed the case; in the later window A06 is itself the final event (median position 1.0) in the traces containing it, and only 3 outgoing transitions from A06 were observed in the whole window, leading to A01 or A04. [DIR006, POS005, POS008, REL042]
- All remaining activities shifted about one event position later: distances from A02 grew by roughly one step (A02→A06 typically 4 steps before vs 5 after, in about 99 vs 97 of 100 cases; A02→A08 4 vs 5; A02→A05 3 vs 4; A02→A07 2 vs 3; A02→A10 and A02→A03 about 2–3 vs 3–4), and A02→A04, previously 1 step in 87 of 100 cases, is now split between 1 step (44 in 100) and 2 steps (47 in 100). [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007]
- Participation of the surviving activities barely moved: A03, A05, A06, A07, A08, A10 and A11 each changed by only about 2.5 in 100 (e.g. A03 45→47.5, A05 55→52.5), a difference random re-splits of a stable process produce routinely (strength about 0.37). [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC008, OCC009]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis of a structural change with two parts: in the later window, A01 is a new mandatory step executed exactly once per case within the first two to three positions — directly after A02 in about half of the cases and after A04 in much of the rest — while A09, which previously always followed A06 and terminated about 45 in 100 cases, is no longer executed, so those cases now end with A06 itself. [OCC001, OCC007, DIR002, DIR004, DIR006, POS001, POS005, POS008, REL042]

Supporting signs: the two anchor differences are far beyond sampling variation (A01 from 0 to 200 of 200 traces; A09 from 90 to 0, each larger than in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits), and the placement evidence agrees across all five indicator families — A02 and A04 now route to A01, A01 precedes every other activity in nearly all shared traces, and every downstream activity (A03, A05, A06, A07, A08, A10) moved about one position later, exactly the pattern an early insertion produces. [OCC001, OCC007, DIR001, DIR002, DIR004, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG007, REL001, REL003]

Limitations: the insertion point is not one fixed edge — A01's successors spread over several activities and the A01/A04 order is mixed (55 vs 45 in 100) — so the evidence locates A01 in the opening steps rather than at a single exact position. What follows A06 in the later window rests on only 3 observed transitions, so an occasional continuation from A06 to A01 or A04 is weakly grounded. Finally, zero participation only shows A09 was not observed; full removal cannot be completely distinguished from execution becoming very rare, although 0 of 200 after 90 of 200 leaves little room for continued regular use. [DIR001, DIR006, REL003, OCC007]

Other differences: participation shifts of about 2.5 in 100 for A03, A05, A06, A07, A08, A10 and A11, and a modest redistribution between A06 and A10 as successors of A03 and A10 (A03→A06 about 58→49 in 100; A10→A06 about 41→47 in 100); these are small and consistent with sampling variation between two 200-trace windows. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, OCC006, OCC008, OCC009, DIR003, DIR010, REL025]
